## Overview

Restoration monitoring on mitigation lands in the Carrizo Plain region of
southeastern San Luis Obispo County. The goal was to detect saltbush from
low-cost drone imagery, so the client could track a restoration plan without
expensive multispectral sensors.

## Approach

The model uses knowledge distillation. A larger "teacher" random forest learns
from a rich set of engineered features: texture measures, color indices, and
principal components. That teacher then trains a lighter "student" model that
runs on RGB-derived features alone, with no extra sensor bands required. The
student reproduces the teacher's classifications with 94.6% agreement while
running on imagery any consumer drone can collect.

## Methods

- Drone RGB imagery at sub-centimeter resolution
- GLCM texture features, vegetation indices, and PCA for the teacher model
- Random forest classification in R
- Repeated cross-validation for model selection
- A reduced 18-feature student model distilled from the teacher's 34 features

## Results

- Teacher model: 34 engineered features (texture, color indices, principal components)
- Student model: 18 RGB-derived features, no extra sensor bands required
- 94.6% agreement between the student and teacher classifications
- 88% within-polygon classification accuracy

## Limitation and next step

RGB-only imagery was the main constraint. Adding a near-infrared band is the
clear next improvement for separating saltbush from spectrally similar
vegetation.
